items.title: Marina Willer crafts letters with light and projection for BFI London Film Festival's new identity
items.summary: Pentagram partner Marina Willer built the BFI London Film Festival's new identity by filming colored light projected against a black screen, capturing letterforms that shift and move. An unusual light blue — no other major film festival uses it — and deep purple anchor the palette.
items.why: Shows how starting from a physical, analogue process generates brand language that digital-first tools simply don't produce — a concrete case for what makes an identity hard to replicate, relevant to Manik's thinking on identity systems with strategic teeth.

items.title: How Coinbase Used Code Connect to Guide Agents and Shrink Token Costs
items.summary: Coinbase's design systems team updated their Figma Code Connect mappings so AI coding agents reference the actual component library rather than guess — cutting token costs by 22% and implementation time by the same margin.
items.why: Makes a quantified case Manik can use at Cuemath: CueDesign documentation quality now directly determines how accurately and cheaply AI agents generate code, turning design system investment into an engineering efficiency argument.

items.title: Ensemble
items.summary: Studio Polytechnic designed the identity for Ensemble — an actor training workshop — using Helvetica Textbook, a rarely chosen variant selected specifically for its "pedagogical feel", with letters arranged in a circular formation that mirrors individual growth within a group.
items.why: Choosing a typeface for its "pedagogical feel" in a learning context is territory Manik works in daily — a precise example of how type selection in education carries meaning well beyond aesthetics.

items.title: How I'm feeling about AI in August 2026
items.summary: GitHub product designer Brian Lovin audits AI tools after daily use: helpful for brainstorming and backend coding, but writing output is "incomprehensibly dumb" and voice modes feel hollow. No hype, no dismissal — a practitioner's running tally.
items.why: The specific split — AI earns its keep in coding, fails at writing — is exactly the calibration Manik needs as he decides where to lean on AI versus where to hold the craft line in his own process.

items.title: Sylvan Hillebrand gives a 125-year-old oil paint company a contemporary refresh
items.summary: Dutch designer Sylvan Hillebrand sharpened Rembrandt's 125-year-old brand identity — updated typefaces, an expanded palette, and a Dutch Golden Age-inspired quality stamp — while managing a gradual rollout across hundreds of products worldwide.
items.why: "Sharpen without reinventing" is the same strategic posture Manik navigates with CueDesign: how to evolve a system while keeping continuity for the users and engineering teams already building on it.
